vulnerability.name: Command Injection
vulnerability.description: Vulnerabilities allowing injection of arbitrary operating system commands
vulnerability.impact: Complete system compromise, data theft, privilege escalation, or service disruption
vulnerability.mitigation: Use parameterized commands, avoid shell execution, validate and sanitize command inputs

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The function 'supportsToken' does not sanitize the user input (the abi encoded packed string), making it vulnerable to command injection.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
```
modifierEntrancy 
  | 
  v 
Bank    
   | 
 supportsToken() --> vulnerable code --> system()```
exploitation_steps: Send a specially crafted input to the 'supportsToken' function
The crafted input is passed to the system() call, executing an arbitrary OS command
findings.remediation: 'supportsToken' function should sanitize user input before passing it to system()

findings.title: Command Injection vulnerability
findings.explanation: The contract allows execution of user-supplied code via msg.sender.call.value(amount), which can lead to Command Injection if the Ethereum node shell (e.g., Geth or Parity) has command injection vulnerabilities.
findings.impact: Complete system compromise, data theft, privilege escalation, or service disruption
exploitation_steps: Send a transaction with the withdraw function
Supply user-defined code in the 'amount' parameter
findings.exploitation_conditions: Attacker can trigger the withdraw function with a malicious payload.
findings.remediation: Replace msg.sender.call.value(amount)() with a secure, parameterized function call that sanitizes and validates input.
